updatewebacl_calls_reading: ZERO, and it is a TRUE ABSENCE rather than an unreadable instrument: the apply never wrote the WebACL at all. Four instruments agree. (1) CloudTrail over 17:10Z-17:33Z returns 21 wafv2 events and NO UpdateWebACL, in a window proven SETTLED by my own five GetWebACL calls on this ACL at 17:14, 17:19, 17:19, 17:23 and 17:25 -- two of them bracketing the apply. (2) The ACL's LockToken is byte-identical before and after (848a6d0b-d69f-40e0-876a-cfc0ce40b6b2); wafv2 re-issues it on every successful update. (3) Capacity is unchanged at 947. (4) rules_sha256 is identical over the whole ordered rule list. Terraform nonetheless logged 'aws_wafv2_web_acl.opal_cloudfront_protection: Modifications complete after 19s' -- a modification it reported and did not send.
updatewebacl_instrument_control: The control that settles it is UpdateIPSet: 2 events in 30 days with eventSource wafv2.amazonaws.com, so THIS TRAIL DOES RECORD wafv2 WRITES and a zero for UpdateWebACL is a real absence. The control I ran BEFORE the apply proved something weaker and I recorded it as sufficient at the time: it showed wafv2 READS (GetWebACL, GetIPSet, ListTagsForResource) reaching the trail, and reads being recorded does not establish that writes are. Same service, different event class.

the_narrowing_measured.reading: the act is exactly a narrowing and nothing more: both paths now refuse an unauthenticated caller and both serve the same 607-byte body to an authenticated one. The bare path answered 200 unauthenticated before this apply.
the_narrowing_measured.refusal_shape: HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, Content-Type application/json, body {"error":"Missing or invalid Authorization header"}, and X-Cache: LambdaGeneratedResponse from cloudfront -- the validator answered at the edge on viewer-request, so a cached 200 cannot be served around it.
